newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Mowlem unveils float plan for SGB unit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mowlem unveils float plan for SGB unit.

text.p: British building group John Mowlem & Co Plc on Wednesday unveiled plans to float off its ladders-to-scaffolding unit SGB Group, a move it said will raise "in excess" of 100 million pounds ($162.7 million).
SGB plans to seek a listing on the London Stock Exchange this summer.

The move to float off part of Mowlem's stake in SGB had been expected. Mowlem has confirmed it will spin off 49 percent of its shares in SGB and use the cash raised to cut debt and to invest in some of its other businesses.

Bob Stokell, chief executive of SGB, said, "As an independent company SGB will be able to develop further an already strong brand name and to exploit the identified opportunities for profit enhancement."

He told Reuters in an interview that the float would raise over 100 million and would be used by the parent group to redeem a 50 million pounds Eurobond and invest in Mowlem's environmental services and facilities management business.
Commenting on the outlook for the independent SGB, the new chief executive told Reuters it would inherit 42 million of debt.

"We are cash generative and so we would expect to reduce that debt and be able to finance modest capital expenditure and acquisitions -- but not within the next 18 months. There will be no deals until the back end of next year (for SGB)," he said.
Until then it will focus on improving existing operations.
Mowlem will seek to place the new company shares with institutional investors and plans to arrange meetings with them over the coming weeks.
Stokell will head the SGB team, with Ken Minton, the chairman of Mowlem itself, chairing the new spin-off company as well.
Stephen Yapp has been appointed SGB's finance director, with Ken Mansell as chief operating officer plus two non-executive directors on the board.
UBS analyst Mark Hake said the floatation had been expected.
"This has been talked about for some time and I think it will be well received in the market. I imagine the company will be valued at up to 130 million pounds," he said.
Mowlem is expected to issue more details of the float later on Wednesday. The group recorded profits of 16 million stg on sales of 263.2 million in the year ended December 31 1996.
The group has worldwide operations including joint ventures in the Far East and Middle East. Most of its business is centred in Britain and continental Europe. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
